items.title: 67247_J.C. Higginbotham oral history interview
items.q: I can tell you I've met Lana Turner and I knew Ella Fitzgerald as a babe. She was only 15 years old.

ctx.x: That's right. We had Sudan Club. I used to work with clubs. I used to get charity. We took care of the hospitals and everything. I was the treasurer of the club and everything. That's before Jay and I ever got married. I know a lot about Harlem. I can tell you more about Harlem than anybody in the world. I came here in 1932... This house, we had doormen, we had elevator men. They didn't allow you to walk up

these stairs. We had everything. But I can tell you the time I met Lena Horne. I can tell you I've met Lana Turner and I knew Ella Fitzgerald as a babe. She was only 15 years old. They don't remember me and I don't want them to remember me, 'cause I worked for a man that even gave Bob Hope his first tuxedo... I'm saying that you can meet these celebrities when they're not nothing and then when they get something they forget about you. You know what I mean? Now I knew Lena Horne down in the village, Cafe Society.
Tell me, Jay C., you were in Europe in the same year in 1958. You were in Europe?
